title: The brain's default mode network
authors: ME Raichle
abstract: Review of the default mode network (DMN) including its relationship to the dorsal attention network (DAN) and its role in brain function and disease.

title: Default-mode network activity distinguishes Alzheimer's disease from healthy aging: evidence from functional MRI
authors: MD Greicius, G Srivastava, AL Reiss et al.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Functional connectivity analysis of fMRI data demonstrating that default-mode network activity distinguishes Alzheimer's disease from healthy aging, with the posterior cingulate cortex as a key node.

title: The connectomics of brain disorders
authors: A Fornito, A Zalesky, M Breakspear
abstract: How network topology can be used to characterize and model vulnerability and resilience to disease and dysfunction, including how network spread relates to higher-order aspects of connectome organization.

title: Is the ADHD brain wired differently? A review on structural and functional connectivity in attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
authors: K Konrad, SB Eickhoff
abstract: Review of brain connectivity models in ADHD, discussing atypical development of neural network integration in subjects with ADHD, similar to disorders such as schizophrenia and autism.

title: Resting state fMRI in Alzheimer's disease: beyond the default mode network
authors: F Agosta, M Pievani, C Geroldi, M Copetti et al.
abstract: Examining connectivity patterns of default mode, frontoparietal, executive, and salience networks in Alzheimer's disease using resting-state fMRI.

title: Brain networks in schizophrenia
authors: MP Van Den Heuvel, A Fornito
abstract: Review discussing recent findings of connectomic studies in schizophrenia that examine how the disorder relates to brain network wiring and dynamics.

title: Dysfunction of large-scale brain networks in schizophrenia: a meta-analysis of resting-state functional connectivity
authors: D Dong, Y Wang, X Chang, C Luo et al.
abstract: Meta-analysis examining dysfunction of large-scale brain networks in schizophrenia, including thalamic connectivity with the ventral attention network nodes.

title: A cross-disorder connectome landscape of brain dysconnectivity
authors: MP Van Den Heuvel, O Sporns
abstract: Review of how connectome alterations in brain disorders relate to each other across disorders, examining biomarkers associated with specific brain disorders and how dysfunction across disorders may relate.

title: Disrupted functional brain connectome in individuals at risk for Alzheimer's disease
authors: J Wang, X Zuo, Z Dai, M Xia, Z Zhao, X Zhao, J Jia et al.
abstract: Examining whole-brain topological organization of the functional connectome in amnestic mild cognitive impairment (aMCI), the prodromal stage of Alzheimer's disease, suggesting connectome-based metrics as disease biomarkers.

title: Age-related changes in the default mode network are more advanced in Alzheimer disease
authors: DT Jones, MM Machulda, P Vemuri, EM McDade et al.
abstract: Comparing default mode network changes in aging versus Alzheimer's disease, showing more advanced alterations in AD compared to normal aging.

title: Shared and distinct intrinsic functional network centrality in autism and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder
authors: A Di Martino, XN Zuo, C Kelly, R Grzadzinski et al.
abstract: Examining common and distinct intrinsic functional network connectivity patterns across ASD and ADHD, two conditions that often exhibit overlapping symptoms.

title: The default mode network in healthy aging and Alzheimer's disease
authors: K Mevel, G Chételat, F Eustache et al.
abstract: Review of default mode network function in healthy aging and Alzheimer's disease, examining the transition from default mode to task-related mode of brain function and altered activity patterns.

title: Brain network connectivity in individuals with schizophrenia and their siblings
authors: G Repovs, JG Csernansky, DM Barch
abstract: Examining functional connectivity within and between the default mode network and three cognitive networks in schizophrenia patients and their siblings, consistent with long-standing hypotheses about schizophrenia.

title: The human connectome in Alzheimer disease—relationship to biomarkers and genetics
authors: M Yu, O Sporns, AJ Saykin
abstract: Connectome studies have provided a theoretical framework, novel quantitative analytic tools and computational network approaches for understanding synaptic impairment in cortical and subcortical brain regions in Alzheimer's disease.

title: Altered default mode network connectivity in Alzheimer's disease—a resting functional MRI and Bayesian network study
authors: X Wu, R Li, AS Fleisher, EM Reiman et al.
abstract: Examining default mode network (DMN) disruption in Alzheimer's disease using resting-state fMRI and Bayesian network analysis to study effective connectivity changes.

title: Brain connectivity in autism
authors: RK Kana, LQ Uddin, T Kenet, D Chugani et al.
abstract: Research topic contributions on brain network connectivity in ASD, underlining the need for understanding connectivity patterns in autism spectrum disorder.

title: A multivariate distance-based analytic framework for connectome-wide association studies
authors: Z Shehzad, C Kelly, PT Reiss, RC Craddock et al.
abstract: A CWAS framework for whole-brain connectivity analysis using multivariate distance-based analytics, accelerating the discovery of brain-behavior relationships in the connectome.

title: Resting state functional connectivity of five neural networks in bipolar disorder and schizophrenia
authors: D Mamah, DM Barch, G Repovs
abstract: Functional dysconnectivity across various brain networks has been reported. We examined neural network dysfunction across multiple networks to understand the relationship between bipolar disorder and schizophrenia.

title: A review of the default mode network in autism spectrum disorders and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
authors: A Harikumar, DW Evans, CC Dougherty et al.
abstract: Review identifying commonalities and differences in default mode network connectivity patterns between ASD and ADHD, given shared connectivity patterns.

title: Shared brain connectivity issues, symptoms, and comorbidities in autism spectrum disorder, attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder, and Tourette syndrome
authors: JK Kern, DA Geier, PG King, LK Sykes et al.
abstract: Proposing that ADHD and TS belong to a broader spectrum of neurodevelopmental illness, an abnormal connectivity spectrum disorder, resulting from neural connectivity abnormalities.

title: Transdiagnostic dysfunctions in brain modules across patients with schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and major depressive disorder: a connectome-based study
authors: Q Ma, Y Tang, F Wang, X Liao, X Jiang et al.
abstract: Using brain network modular architecture, we investigated whole-brain network modular properties and connection patterns across schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and major depressive disorder.

title: Structural brain connectome and cognitive impairment in Parkinson disease
authors: S Galantucci, F Agosta, E Stefanova, S Basaia et al.
abstract: Whole-brain connectome analysis with diffusion tensor MRI in Parkinson disease reveals structural brain connectome alterations associated with cognitive impairment.

title: Connectome biomarkers of drug-resistant epilepsy
authors: S Larivière, A Bernasconi, N Bernasconi et al.
abstract: Structural connectome and hippocampal biomarkers for prediction of cognitive impairment including memory dysfunction in drug-resistant epilepsy.

title: The compensatory phenomenon of the functional connectome related to pathological biomarkers in individuals with subjective cognitive decline
authors: Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative
abstract: Subjective cognitive decline (SCD) might serve as the typical preclinical stage along the AD continuum, with functional network compensatory phenomena related to pathological biomarkers.

title: Impact of the resolution of brain parcels on connectome-wide association studies in fMRI
authors: P Bellec, Y Benhajali, F Carbonell, C Dansereau et al.
abstract: Investigating the impact of functional brain parcel resolution on CWAS results, ranging from large to fine-grained parcellations using generalized linear models of connectomes.
